title: Generic direct-image exchange over an arbitrary algebraically closed base
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field, $N\geq1$ an integer invertible in $F$, and $A$ a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$. Let $B$ be a smooth integral finite-type $F$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $Q=F(B)$ be the fraction field of the coordinate ring of a nonempty affine open of $B$, let $L/Q$ be an algebraically closed algebraic field extension, and for any $B$-scheme $W$ put $W_L=W\times_B\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $g_W:W_L\to W$ [def-pc-base-change]. If $h:T\to Y$ is a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of finite-type $B$-schemes and $E\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, then the canonical unbounded adjunction-mate exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{h,E}:g_Y^*Rh_*E\longrightarrow Rh_{L,*}g_T^*E$$
is an isomorphism. Here quasi-compact and quasi-separated mean that inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact and the diagonal is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]; $h_L:T_L\to Y_L$ is the base change of $h$. The canonical exchange agrees with the composite of the exchanges for the ordinary generic projection $\operatorname{Spec}Q\to B$ and the field extension $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}Q$, under the canonical composite-functor identifications [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Scheme inverse images on these categories are exact constant-coefficient inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

source.place: Tags 0F09 (lemma-smooth-base-change-general) and 0F1C (lemma-base-change-field-extension); agent geometric-generic specialization and constant-module transport.

proof.text: Identify the chosen fraction field Q with B.functionField using IsLocalization.algEquiv and [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. The equality of the algebra maps identifies Spec Q -> B with B.fromSpecFunctionField. For the generic-point specialization of [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods], use the already proved source theorem Scheme.isLimitFunctionFieldCone, with its nonempty affine opens and affine transition maps. Whisker its cone by the order-dual equivalence and transport its vertex along Spec Q ≅ Spec B.functionField. Scheme.fromSpecFunctionField_eq_functionFieldCone_comp verifies the prescribed projections to B.

source.place: Tags 0F09, lemma-smooth-base-change-general: choice of limiting base; geometry from Tags 01RV and 0GWT

proof.text: Since B is locally of finite type over the Noetherian scheme Spec F, it is locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. The affine stage maps are open immersions and hence smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], quasi-separated, and quasi-compact because their sources are affine and B is quasi-separated, as in [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Their pullbacks to Y remain smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Lift the cone into Over B, apply Over.pullback Y.hom, and then Over.forget Y. The first functor is a right adjoint and the second preserves connected limits; the directed index category is connected. This constructs Y ×_B Spec Q as the limit without a separate geometric limit-fibre-products theorem. Pullback symmetry puts its vertex on the specified corners. Affine transitions follow by stability of IsAffineHom under pullback. All property assertions here use the existing Mathlib instances directly.

source.place: Tag 0F09, lemma-smooth-base-change-general: smooth qcqs stages and affine transitions; geometry Tags 01T6, 01OY, 01VC, 01VA, 01V7 and 01YW

proof.text: Write $U_WE$ for the underlying abelian derived object. The exact coefficient-forgetting functor, its commutation with cohomology, and its conservativity are supplied by [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison]. Since $NA=0$, every stalk of every cohomology sheaf of $U_TE$ is killed by $N$. Moreover $N$ is a unit on $B$, on $Y$, and on every base change: its inverse is the image of $N^{-1}\in F$. The object $U_TE$ is bounded below. Apply [lem-kun-0f09] with base $S=Y$, morphism $f=h$, stages $S_i=Y_i$, and limit $S'=Y_Q$. Step 2 verifies all stage hypotheses, and $h$ is qcqs by assumption. It gives that the canonical abelian bounded-below exchange to $Q$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-agrees], the canonical unbounded abelian exchange is the same map through the canonical bounded-below inclusions and direct-image comparisons. Finally [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison] identifies the forgotten module exchange with this abelian exchange through its two endpoint isomorphisms. Conservativity therefore proves that the canonical module exchange $g_{Y,Q}^*Rh_*E\to Rh_{Q,*}g_{T,Q}^*E$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F09, lemma-smooth-base-change-general; coefficient forgetting and bounded-below/unbounded comparison as in the cited nodes

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), $h_Q:T_Q\to Y_Q$ is qcqs. Set $E_Q=g_{T,Q}^*E$. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3) keeps it bounded below, and $N$ still annihilates its cohomology. Forget coefficients as in step 3. Apply [lem-kun-0f1c-exchange] to $h_Q$, the field extension $L/Q$, and the underlying abelian object of $E_Q$. Its torsion hypothesis holds since $N$ is a unit in $Q$; this lemma allows arbitrary extensions, so no separability of $L/Q$ is imposed. It asserts that the canonical bounded-below abelian exchange is an isomorphism. Use [lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-agrees] and then the endpoint-isomorphism identity and conservativity in [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison], exactly as in step 3. The result is invertibility of the specified unbounded module exchange for $h_Q$ and $L/Q$. This square has the chosen corners $(Y_Q)_L=Y_Q\times_{\operatorname{Spec}Q}\operatorname{Spec}L$, $(T_Q)_L$. Let $\square_2=(h_Q,h_L,k,k_1)$, with $k=1_Y\times_B(\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}Q):Y_L\to Y_Q$ and $k_1$ likewise; by [def-pc-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] it is cartesian, and the unique $Y_Q$- and $L$-morphisms $\varphi_Y:Y_L\to(Y_Q)_L$, $\varphi_T:T_L\to(T_Q)_L$ are isomorphisms with $(h_Q)_L\varphi_T=\varphi_Yh_L$. So $\square_2$ is the square $\square_\varphi=((h_Q)_L,h_L,\varphi_Y,\varphi_T)$ pasted onto the 0F1C square $(h_Q,(h_Q)_L,r_{Y_Q},r_{T_Q})$, as $r_{Y_Q}\varphi_Y=k$ and $r_{T_Q}\varphi_T=k_1$. Inverse images along the isomorphisms $\varphi$ are equivalences, with quasi-inverses the inverse images along $\varphi^{-1}$, by the composition and identity isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2), (3), applied termwise. Hence $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square_\varphi}$ is invertible by [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences], and [lem-fin-module-exchange-composite-base-change] shows that $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square_2}$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0F1C, lemma-base-change-field-extension, including its purely inseparable reduction

proof.text: Paste the cartesian square $\square_1$ for $Y_Q\to Y$ (step 3) and the square $\square_2$ for $k:Y_L\to Y_Q$ (step 4). Since $g_{Y,Q}\circ k=g_Y$ and $g_{T,Q}\circ k_1=g_T$ by [def-pc-base-change], the outer rectangle is literally the square $(h,h_L,g_Y,g_T)$ of the statement; only the commutativity enters the exchange through $\theta_\square$. By [lem-fin-module-exchange-composite-base-change], the canonical exchange for this rectangle is, under the specified inverse-image composition isomorphisms, the pullback by $k$ of the exchange in step 3 followed by the exchange for $\square_2$ in step 4. Both factors are isomorphisms: any functor preserves an inverse, and a composite of invertible arrows is invertible. Hence $\operatorname{Ex}_{h,E}$ is an isomorphism. The same pasting identity proves the final compatibility clause, for these canonical mates and not merely for some isomorphism of their endpoints.

The mathematics is correct. The statement is a true composite of 0F09 at the generic point and 0F1C for L/Q. I tested it with N=1, E=0, T empty, h an identity or open immersion, the nonseparated doubled-origin curve, and inseparable L/Q. All hypotheses are met: B is Noetherian and quasi-separated; the U_i->B are smooth and qcqs, and so are their base changes Y_i; limit-fibre-products gives Y_Q as the limit with affine transitions; N^{-1} lies in Gamma(Y,O_Y) and N is a unit in Q; inverse image is exact, so E_Q stays in D^+. Invertibility passes from the abelian maps to the module maps through t∘U(Ex)=Ex∘s and conservativity, without identifying coefficient categories. There is no cycle and no duplicate (lem-weil-geometric-generic-exchange, lem-sc-*-direct-image-exchange and lem-kun-0f1c are weaker or different). No new nodes. Two repairs, in fixes/.../lem-sf-etale-generic-direct-image-exchange.json. (1) B3: the item's exchange is the unbounded module mate, but only def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange was cited; I added [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] to the statement and stmt_deps (citation only). (2) E5: 0F1C is stated for the corners (Y_Q)x_Q L and (T_Q)_L, which differ from the statement's chosen Y x_B L and T_L; step 5 had identified the squares without argument. Step 4 now defines the square for k:Y_L->Y_Q, cartesian by pasting, and shows its exchange is invertible: the square along the corner isomorphisms has invertible exchange by lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences and lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition (2),(3), then lem-fin-module-exchange-composite-base-change applies. Step 5 now pastes literally to the statement's square. proof_deps recomputed.
